extraction.narrative:
# DISCHARGE SUMMARY

**PATIENT INFORMATION**
Name: John Smith
Age: 65 years
Gender: Male
Medical Record Number: 12345

Admission Date: January 15, 2024
Surgery Date: January 16, 2024
Discharge Date: January 19, 2024
Length of Stay: 4 days

---

**DIAGNOSES**

Primary Diagnosis: Right frontal brain lesion

---

**HOSPITAL COURSE**

Mr. Smith is a 65-year-old male who presented to the hospital on January 15, 2024, with severe headaches and mild right-sided weakness. On admission, neurological examination revealed a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 15 with full orientation and right arm weakness graded at 4+/5 strength.

The patient underwent right frontal craniotomy on January 16, 2024, for resection of the lesion. The procedure was performed without documented intraoperative complications.

Post-operatively, the patient's course was uncomplicated. By the time of discharge on post-operative day 3, neurological examination demonstrated significant improvement. The patient was alert and oriented to person, place, and time, moving all extremities with good strength. The previously noted right arm weakness had improved to 5-/5 strength, representing near-complete resolution of the pre-operative motor deficit.

---

**DISCHARGE STATUS**

Neurological Status: Glasgow Coma Scale 15. Alert and oriented x3. Moving all extremities with good strength. Mild residual right arm weakness improved to 5-/5.

Functional Status: Karnofsky Performance Status 80, modified Rankin Scale 1, ECOG Performance Status 1. The patient demonstrates normal activity with minimal effort and no significant disability.

---

**DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS**

1. Levetiracetam (Keppra) 1000 mg by mouth twice daily
2. Dexamethasone 4 mg by mouth every 6 hours with taper

---

**FOLLOW-UP**

Follow-up arrangements and activity restrictions were not documented in the available clinical data. The patient should follow up as directed by the neurosurgical team.
